spec_features.spec_quote: Set MAX_TURNS = 50 as the upper limit.
spec_features.evidence: experiment_config.py:13 `MAX_TURNS = 50`; experiment_harness.py:355 `for turn_num in range(1, MAX_TURNS + 1):` bounds the session loop and it terminates after 50 turns. Imported at experiment_harness.py:16.
spec_features.notes: The loop range actually reads and enforces the constant, so the cap is end-to-end enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Without a limit, pathological loops could run indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: experiment_harness.py:355 `for turn_num in range(1, MAX_TURNS + 1)` is finite, so a loop cannot run indefinitely. MAX_TURNS=50 at experiment_config.py:13.
spec_features.notes: Identical enforced mechanism as feature 1 (the bounded loop). No separate code element.

spec_features.spec_quote: Could stop after detecting "give up," but simpler to keep fixed
spec_features.evidence: Spec frames this as rejected, but the code DOES implement it: experiment_harness.py:251-253 detects 'give up'/'can't'/'cannot' + fix/debug/solve and sets `action_type = TurnType.GIVE_UP`; experiment_harness.py:366-368 `if turn.action_type == TurnType.GIVE_UP: gave_up_turn = turn_num; break` halts the loop early.
spec_features.notes: Detection is narrow (substring/regex match on response text) but it is wired and honored as a real early stop, exceeding the spec's stated 'keep fixed' choice.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gave_up_turn = turn_num  (the break records a metric and stops once the subject quits; no welfare comment)
